answer: To blunt Sybil attacks, a mining protocol can make each identity sit on a proof-of-work knoll: a new account must solve a per-epoch puzzle whose difficulty scales with how many keys share the same funding source or IP cluster, so the next identity never costs less than the last. An attacker racing real users at the dawn of an epoch pays the same energy and capital for every fake account, and their onyx deposit gets diluted, so mass registration loses money before it can claim emission. Honest miners still pass with one seat, while a swarm of alts faces rising cost per vote.
